decidedBy: Essenthos, 2026-09-27, on the portrait briefs' report of records holding several people, on the names a mapping crossed in the translations, and on the pairing of the two lists of Nehemiah 12, each occurrence read against its verse by claude-opus-5-5
policy: A record is one person, and a word names the one its verse names. Where a translation's word was given the other name of its verse, the word is given its own; where an earlier ruling paired the wrong house of a list, it is corrected and says which ruling it corrects; and where a record held the verses of another man or woman of the name, the occurrences the verse settles are given to the person it names.

Nehemiah 12:12-21 names the heads of the priestly houses of 12:1-7 in the same order. 'Of Joiarib, Mattenai; of Jedaiah, Uzzi' follows 12:6, 'Joiarib, Jedaiah', whose Jedaiah the lexicon enumerates with 1 Chronicles 9:10 and Nehemiah 7:39. The review of 2026-09-06 argued the same pairing and named the Jedaiah of 12:7.

Nehemiah 12:12-21 names the heads of the priestly houses of 12:1-7 in the same order. 'Of Hilkiah, Hashabiah; of Jedaiah, Nethaneel' follows 12:7, 'Hilkiah, Jedaiah', whose Jedaiah the lexicon enumerates with Nehemiah 11:10. The review of 2026-09-06 argued the same pairing and named the Jedaiah of 12:6.

Matthew 13:55 asks 'is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas?': they are named as Jesus's brothers, and the verse names Mary as Jesus's mother, not as theirs.

'And there was Mary Magdalene, and the other Mary, sitting over against the sepulchre': 'Mary Magdalene, and the other Mary' — the mother of James and Joses (MAT 27:56, MRK 15:40), whom the verses name beside Mary Magdalene and never as Jesus's mother.

'came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary to see the sepulchre': 'Mary Magdalene, and the other Mary' — the mother of James and Joses (MAT 27:56, MRK 15:40), whom the verses name beside Mary Magdalene and never as Jesus's mother.
'Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the less and of Joses, and Salome': the second Mary is the mother of James and Joses.
'Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses beheld where he was laid': the second Mary is the mother of Joses.
'Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James, and Salome': the second Mary is the mother of James.
'Mary Magdalene, and Joanna, and Mary the mother of James': the third woman is the mother of James.
'his mother, and his mother's sister, Mary the wife of Cleophas, and Mary Magdalene': the first Mary named is Mary of Clopas.
'Mary the wife of Cleophas, and Mary Magdalene': the second Mary named is Mary Magdalene.

'the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found him in the way': the prophet of Shiloh, who tore his garment in twelve pieces for Jeroboam. The priest Ahiah son of Ahitub of 1 Samuel 14:3 and 14:18, Saul's day, is another man and has his own record.

says.distinguisher: a chief of the priests who came up with Zerubbabel (NEH 12:1, 12:7)

rulings.why: 'Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, Jedaiah. These were the chief of the priests' who came up with Zerubbabel (12:1). The high priest of Josiah's day, the Hilkiah beside Ezra and Gemariah's father each have their own record.
'Of Hilkiah, Hashabiah': the house of the Hilkiah of 12:7, in the order of the first list.

says.notes: King of Persia. In his second year Haggai and Zechariah prophesied and the building of the house of God at Jerusalem resumed (Ezra 4:24; Haggai 1:1; Zechariah 1:1); he had Cyrus's decree searched out at Achmetha and confirmed it (Ezra 6:1-12), and the house was finished in his sixth year (Ezra 6:15).

rulings.why: 'In the second year of Darius the king': the king in whose second year the building of the house of God resumed (EZR 4:24), who searched out Cyrus's decree and confirmed it (EZR 6:1-12), and in whose sixth year the house was finished (EZR 6:15).
